items.en: A stamp museum that opened last month is proving a hit with the public. In the museum's history room you can take in the history of the postage stamp at a glance. In the children's hands-on room you can smell scented stamps or handle wooden ones. You can also make a stamp of your own with your photograph set into it. And the museum's "slow postbox" — write a letter, drop it in, and receive it a year later — is drawing a crowd of its own.
items.why:
Option 2 is the passage's fourth sentence with nothing changed. 자신의 사진이 들어간 우표도 직접 만들 수 있다 and 직접 우표를 만들어 볼 수 있다 say the same thing; the only difference is -아/어 보다 added to the verb, which does not change what is on offer. On a prose passage the right option is usually the one sentence rewritten rather than the one summarised.

Option 1 takes a number out of the wrong sentence. The museum 지난달 문을 열었다 — it opened last month. 일 년 appears in the passage, but it belongs to the postbox: 일 년 뒤에 받아 볼 수 있는. Lifting a figure from one sentence and attaching it to another is the commonest move this type makes on prose, and it works because the number really is on the page.

Option 3 negates a verb the passage states. 나무 우표 등을 만져 볼 수 있다 says the wooden stamps in the 체험실 can be handled, and 만질 수 없다 says they cannot. An option carrying 없다 or 못하다 is worth taking straight to the verb it denies; a passage this short will usually have said it outright.

Option 4 does the same to the postbox. 편지를 써서 넣으면 … 받아 볼 수 있는 describes writing a letter, posting it, and getting it back a year later, so 편지를 보내지 못한다 contradicts the first half of that sentence. Note that the sentence is doing two things at once — you send and you receive — and the option denies only one of them, which is what makes it read as plausible.

Every option here maps onto exactly one sentence and no sentence is used twice. That is the structure to exploit on a passage: read the five sentences first, then take each option to the single sentence it belongs to rather than re-reading the whole thing four times. The second sentence — the 역사실 — is the one no option touches, and a passage always prints more than it asks about.
items.grammar:
문을 열다 is to open the door, and of a shop or a museum it is to open for business. 지난달 문을 연 우표 박물관 puts it on the modifier: 열다 is a ㄹ-stem, so -(으)ㄴ drops the ㄹ and gives 연. The opposite is 문을 닫다, which likewise means to close down rather than to shut a door.

-아/어 보다 is trying something out, and this passage uses it three times — 맡거나, 만져 볼 수 있다, 받아 볼 수 있다 — because that is what a 체험실 is for. It is also why option 2 can add 볼 to 만들 수 있다 without changing the claim: 만들 수 있다 and 만들어 볼 수 있다 both mean you are allowed to make one.

나다 is the verb for something coming off a thing — a smell, a sound, a fever. 향기(가) 나다 is to give off a scent, so 향기 나는 우표 is a scented stamp. And 들어가다 is to go in: 사진이 들어간 우표 is a stamp with a photograph set into it, where the thing that went in takes 이/가 rather than 을/를.

느린 우체통 is a real fixture in Korea rather than an invention of this paper — you post a letter and it is delivered a year later. 인기를 끌다 is to pull in popularity, so 인기를 끌고 있다 is to be drawing a crowd right now; it sits alongside 인기가 있다 and 인기가 많다.

한눈에 is in a single glance, and 한눈에 볼 수 있다 is the standard phrase for a display that lets you take everything in at once. 써서 is 쓰다 plus -아/어서 in its sequence sense — write it, and then put it in — and 넣으면 is the condition that the rest of the sentence answers.

items.phraseKo: 휴일에 산을 오르던 경찰이 등산객을 구조했다.

lines.ko: 휴일에 산을 오르던 경찰이 등산객을 구조했다.
지난 1일 김민수 경위는 인주산 정상에서 한 여성이 쓰러져 있는 것을 발견했다.
김 경위는 바로 여성의 체온이 떨어지지 않게 겉옷을 벗어서 덮어 주고 119에 신고했다.
이후 김 경위는 구조대 차량이 올 수 있는 산 중턱 대피소까지 여성을 업고 뛰어 내려갔다.
병원으로 이송된 여성은 치료를 받고 건강을 되찾았다.

choices.ko: 한 등산객이 산 정상에 쓰러져 있었다.
김 경위는 등산객의 신고를 받고 산에 올라갔다.

items.en: A policeman out climbing on his day off rescued a hiker. On the 1st, Lieutenant Kim Min-su found a woman lying collapsed at the summit of Mount Inju. He at once took off his coat and covered her so that her body temperature would not drop, and called 119. He then carried her on his back and ran down to the shelter halfway up the mountain, as far as a rescue vehicle could come. Taken on to hospital, the woman was treated and recovered her health.
items.why:
Option 1 is the second sentence with one word exchanged, and the first sentence is what licenses the exchange. 인주산 정상에서 한 여성이 쓰러져 있는 것을 발견했다 says a woman was lying collapsed at the summit; 경찰이 등산객을 구조했다, one sentence earlier, has already told you that the person rescued was a hiker. Carrying 등산객 = 여성 across from sentence one to sentence two is the whole of what this question asks.

Option 2 gives 김 경위 the vehicle. 구조대 차량이 올 수 있는 산 중턱 대피소 is a long modifier on 대피소 — the shelter is as high as a rescue vehicle can reach — and the officer himself 업고 뛰어 내려갔다, carrying her on his back on foot. A noun buried under a relative clause is where this type puts the thing it means to swap.

Option 3 changes the actor and the destination at once. It was 김 경위 who carried her, not the 구조대, and he carried her to the 대피소, not to the hospital. The hospital comes in the last sentence and by a different means: 병원으로 이송된 여성 — she was transported there, which is what the rescue team did after the shelter. Either change alone would sink the option; having both is what makes it read like a summary.

Option 4 reverses the direction of the report. 휴일에 산을 오르던 경찰 puts the officer on the mountain on his own time, and it was he who 119에 신고했다. 등산객의 신고를 받고 산에 올라갔다 makes him an officer answering a call and going up in response — an ordinary story, and not this one. 휴일 in the first sentence is there precisely to rule it out.

The passage is a chain of actions with one actor each, and every wrong option moves an action to the wrong actor or the wrong place. So the quick read is to list who did what before looking at the options at all: 김 경위 found her, covered her, called 119, and carried her down to the shelter; the 구조대 took her on to hospital. Four facts, and three of the four options fall out of them.
items.grammar:
-던 marks an action that was under way at the time: 산을 오르던 경찰 is a policeman in the middle of a climb, not one who climbs. It is what makes 휴일에 do its work — he was off duty and out walking rather than on patrol, which is the fact option 4 needs you to have missed.

-아/어 있다 is a state left standing after an action finishes, not an action in progress. 쓰러져 있다 is lying collapsed; 앉아 있다 is seated. 쓰러지고 있다 would be falling over at that moment, which is a different picture and not what anyone finds at a summit.

-지 않게 states the purpose the next action serves. 체온이 떨어지지 않게 겉옷을 벗어서 덮어 주고 is one continuous act built out of three verbs: -아/어서 is sequence (take it off, and then), -아/어 주다 is doing it for her rather than for himself, and -고 carries on to the next thing he did.

업다 is to carry on your back, and it is worth keeping apart from 안다, which is in your arms, and 들다, which is in your hands. 뛰어 내려가다 stacks two directions of travel on each other — running, and going down — the way Korean regularly does with movement verbs.

이송되다 is the passive of 이송하다 and belongs to hospital and emergency reporting rather than to conversation: 병원으로 이송되다 is the phrase a news item uses. And 되찾다 carries the prefix 되-, which puts back or again on a verb: 되찾다 to get back and 되살리다 to bring back to life.

exercises.instructionKo: 다음을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것을 고르십시오.
exercises.instructionEn: Choose the correct order for the sentences.
exercises.blurbEn: Four sentences out of order and four orderings — but the sentence that can open, and one connective, usually settle it.
exercises.noteEn:
Four sentences printed out of order, four orderings offered, and the options do a good deal of the work for you. Read what they propose as the first sentence before reading the sentences themselves; that alone usually leaves two.

The opening sentence is the one that needs nothing in front of it. It names its subject with 은/는 instead of pointing back at one, and it carries no connective at all. A sentence that begins 그래서, 그런데, 따라서, 이후 or 그 is out of first place before you have read what it says.

Connectives then pin sentences to each other, and two pins usually finish the ordering. 그래서 and 따라서 need a cause standing in front of them. 그런데 needs something to turn against. 오히려 needs an expectation, stated earlier, that it can overturn.

도 and 까지 mark an addition, so a sentence carrying either cannot be the first of the things being added. 것도 장점이다 is a second advantage, so the first one is somewhere above it. 거절하는 경우까지 발생한다 is the far end of a problem, so the ordinary case comes before.

A conclusion goes last. 따라서 … 해야 한다 is advice drawn from everything above it, and advice placed in the middle would be advice about nothing yet said.

Where a paragraph also runs on a clock — 밤새, 아침에 — check that the time words and the connectives agree. When they do you can stop reading; when they do not, you have misread one of them, and it is nearly always the connective.

items.phraseKo: 신비 복숭아는 2017년에 한국에 처음 소개된 여름 과일이다.

lines.ko: 그래서 껍질째 먹기도 편하고 딱딱하지 않아서 식감도 좋다.
신비 복숭아는 2017년에 한국에 처음 소개된 여름 과일이다.
다른 복숭아에 비해 이른 시기에 먹을 수 있다는 것도 장점이다.
껍질이 얇은 복숭아와 속이 부드러운 복숭아의 장점을 결합해 만들었다.

items.en: The Sinbi peach is a summer fruit first introduced to Korea in 2017. It was made by combining the strengths of a thin-skinned peach and a soft-fleshed one. So it is easy to eat skin and all, and it is not hard, so the texture is good too. That it can be eaten earlier in the season than other peaches is a further advantage.
items.why:
(나) is the only sentence that can open. It names its subject and says what it is — 신비 복숭아는 … 여름 과일이다 — with nothing pointing back at anything. (라) has no subject of its own, (가) begins 그래서, and (다) says 것도, which needs an advantage above it. Three of the four options open with (나) even so, so this only removes ③.

그래서 pins (가) to whatever explains it, and (라) is that explanation. (가) says the peach is easy to eat skin and all and is not hard; (라) says it was made by combining a thin-skinned peach with a soft-fleshed one. Thin skin gives 껍질째, soft flesh gives 딱딱하지 않아서. So (라) comes immediately before (가), and only ① does that.

(다) confirms the reading rather than deciding it. 것도 장점이다 marks a further advantage, so an advantage has to have been given already, and the advantages are in (가). A sentence carrying 도 is almost never the first of the things it is adding to.

Notice what does not decide this one. 2017년 and 처음 look like the start of a chronology, but no other sentence is dated, so there is no timeline to sort. The joins here are logical, and the year is only there to make (나) sound like an opening — which it is, for a different reason.
items.grammar:
N째 means without removing it: 껍질째 is skin and all, 통째로 is whole, 그릇째 is dish and all. It attaches straight to the noun with no particle.

N에 비해 is compared with N, and it takes a noun and never a clause — 다른 복숭아에 비해. To compare with a whole clause you need -(으)ㄴ 것에 비해 instead.

이르다 here is to be early, and its modifier is 이른 시기. Keep it apart from the other 이르다, to reach, which comes out 이르러 and belongs to different sentences entirely.

먹을 수 있다는 것도 장점이다 turns a whole clause into a noun with -다는 것 and then marks it 도. That 도 is the piece of grammar the ordering actually turns on: it says another advantage has already been given.

결합해 만들었다 chains two verbs with -아/어: they combined them and made it. 결합하다 is to join two things into one thing, which is stronger than 합치다.

items.phraseKo: 아이가 감기에 걸려 밤새 큰 소리로 울었다.

lines.ko: 아이가 감기에 걸려 밤새 큰 소리로 울었다.
아주머니는 아이가 많이 아팠냐며 오히려 걱정해 주셨다.
아침에 아이와 병원에 가려고 집을 나서다 옆집 아주머니를 만났다.
나는 우는 아이를 달래면서도 울음소리에 이웃들이 깰까 봐 걱정했다.

items.en: My child caught a cold and cried loudly all night. I soothed the crying child, and all the while worried that the sound would wake the neighbours. In the morning, as I was leaving the house to take the child to the doctor, I ran into the lady next door. She asked whether the child had been very ill — if anything, she was worried for us.
items.why:
(가) is the only sentence with no thread running back to another. It sets the scene: the child caught a cold and cried all night. (나) opens with 아주머니는, a person nobody has introduced yet; (다) is where she is introduced; (라) begins 나는 우는 아이를, which needs the crying already on the page. So (가) is first, and ③ and ④ go together.

That leaves whether (나) or (라) comes second, and (나) cannot: it is the neighbour replying, and she has not been met yet. The meeting is in (다), so (다) must stand before (나) — which only ② does. One sentence naming a person and another one introducing them is the commonest single clue in this type.

오히려 confirms it. It overturns an expectation, and the expectation is in (라): the speaker feared the neighbours would be woken and put out. 오히려 걱정해 주셨다 — she was worried for them instead. An 오히려 sentence always points back at a fear or an assumption someone has already stated.

The paragraph also runs on a clock — 밤새, then 아침에 — and the clock agrees with the logic. When the time words and the connectives agree you can stop checking. When they disagree, you have misread one of them.
items.grammar:
감기에 걸리다 is to catch a cold, and 걸리다 takes 에 for the illness. The same verb is 시간이 걸리다, to take time, so the particle carries more of the meaning here than the verb does.

아팠냐며 is -냐고 하며 worn down: asking whether it was so, and going on to do something else in the same breath. It reports a question inside a narrative without stopping to quote it, which is why it reads as one continuous action with 걱정해 주셨다.

오히려 is on the contrary, if anything. It needs an expectation to work against, and it is worth treating as a pointer: whatever it overturns is in an earlier sentence.

-(으)면서도 is while doing, and yet. 달래면서도 걱정했다 is two things at once that pull against each other. Drop the 도 and it is simply while, with no tension in it.

-(으)ㄹ까 봐 is for fear that. 깰까 봐 걱정했다 puts the feared thing in front and the reaction behind, and it only ever takes a verb of worrying, avoiding or preparing.

items.phraseKo: 최근 온라인 가구 구매가 늘면서 반품 사례가 많아지고 있다.

lines.ko: 최근 온라인 가구 구매가 늘면서 반품 사례가 많아지고 있다.
그런데 비싼 반품 비용으로 인해 피해를 보는 소비자가 늘고 있다.
따라서 소비자는 구매 전에 반품 비용과 조건을 잘 확인해야 한다.
업체가 까다로운 조건을 내세워 반품을 거절하는 경우까지 발생한다.

items.en: Online furniture buying has risen lately, and with it the number of returns. But the cost of returning an item is high, and more and more consumers are losing out by it. There are even cases of firms setting demanding conditions and refusing the return outright. Consumers should therefore check the cost and the terms of returns before they buy.
items.why:
(가) is the general situation and the only sentence that can state one. It carries no connective and introduces both nouns the rest depends on — 온라인 가구 구매 and 반품. (나) opens 그런데, (다) opens 따라서, and (라) describes a case that only means anything once a problem exists. Two of the four options open with (라), so reading nothing but the first sentence removes ③ and ④ together.

따라서 goes last, and that finishes it. It draws advice — 확인해야 한다 — from what came before, and advice placed in the middle of a paragraph would be advice about nothing yet said. ② puts (다) third and leaves (나) at the end, so the conclusion is buried and the 그런데 problem trails after it. That leaves ①.

The remaining join runs by degree. (나) is the problem: returns cost so much that consumers lose out. (라) is worse than that — 거절하는 경우까지 발생한다, where 까지 says this is the far end of it. An escalation follows the thing it escalates from and never precedes it.

그런데 in (나) wants something neutral to turn against, and (가) is exactly that: a rising trend, stated without comment. Fact, then a 그런데 problem, then a worse case, then a 따라서 conclusion — a great many of these paragraphs are built on that frame, and recognising it is worth more than reading all four sentences closely.
items.grammar:
-(으)면서 here is not one person doing two things but one change accompanying another: 구매가 늘면서 반품 사례가 많아지고 있다, as buying rises, returns rise with it. That use belongs to written Korean and turns up constantly in this kind of paragraph.

(으)로 인해 is owing to, and it is the formal cause connector — 비싼 반품 비용으로 인해. It attaches to a noun, where -아/어서 attaches to a clause, and the paper prefers it in anything argumentative.

피해를 보다 is to suffer harm. 보다 collocates with 피해, 손해 and 이익: in Korean you see a loss rather than take one. 피해를 주다 is the other side of it, to do the harm.

까지 is as far as, even. 거절하는 경우까지 발생한다 pushes the claim to its extreme, which is exactly why that sentence cannot come first among the problems it belongs to.

따라서 is therefore in writing; 그래서 is its spoken twin. 따라서 introduces the conclusion of an argument rather than the result of an event, which is why it so reliably marks the last sentence of a paragraph like this one.

exercises.instructionKo: ( )에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르십시오.
exercises.instructionEn: Choose the phrase that best fits the blank.
exercises.blurbEn: A short passage with one phrase cut out of it. The vocabulary is not the question — what fills the gap is whatever the rest of the paragraph has been arguing for.
exercises.noteEn:
Four or five sentences and one phrase removed, usually from the last of them. Unlike the 빈칸 of 문항 1-2, where four endings sit on the same verb, here the options are four different ideas and the grammar is nearly always already correct. So the question is not what fits the sentence but what the paragraph has spent its other sentences establishing.

Read the sentence the blank is in first, and read it to the end. The words after the gap decide more than the words before it: 못한다 means the blank is part of a failure, 정도로 means it is being measured against the clause in front, 수 있다 means it is an ability the passage has been explaining.

Then find the sentence that gives the reason. These paragraphs are built as a claim followed by its ground, or a ground followed by its conclusion, and the blank is nearly always one half of that pair. If the last sentence recommends something, the blank is the problem the recommendation answers; if the passage measures a weight, the blank is what the weight proves.

The wrong options come in three shapes worth knowing on sight.

1. True of the subject but absent from the passage. An arctic fox does keep warm by its fur, and 체온을 유지하다 is a fact about foxes — but the passage is about colour, and colour does not warm anything. This is the trap that catches people who know the topic.

2. Brought in from outside knowledge. 청동기 시대 makes anyone think of bronze weapons, and an option about making weapons is waiting for exactly that. The passage argues only from the weight of the stones; nothing else may be used.

3. The right idea pointing the wrong way. 빠르게 줄이지 못한다 names the muscle and the change, and reverses which of them is failing. Check the direction of every option that uses the passage's own words.

items.phraseKo: 북극여우는 계절에 따라 털 색깔을 바꾸는 동물이다.

lines.ko: 북극여우는 계절에 따라 털 색깔을 바꾸는 동물이다.
북극여우의 털은 겨울에는 눈과 같은 흰색으로, 여름에는 바위나 흙과 비슷한 갈색빛으로 바뀐다.
이러한 털 색깔의 변화로 북극여우는 몸을 숨길 곳이 없는 북극의 특수한 환경에서도 천적으로부터 자신을 보호하고 사냥할 때 {} 수 있다.

items.en: The arctic fox is an animal that changes the colour of its coat with the season. Its fur turns white as snow in winter and a brown close to rock and soil in summer. That change of colour lets the arctic fox protect itself from predators even in the bare Arctic, where there is nowhere to hide — and get close to its prey unnoticed when it hunts.
items.why:
The whole passage is about one mechanism: a coat the colour of whatever is behind it. White against snow, brown against rock and soil. Camouflage does two jobs and the sentence names them both — 천적으로부터 자신을 보호하고, and then the blank, under 사냥할 때. Being unseen while hunting is getting close to prey without being noticed, which is ②.

하고 is what pins it. 보호하고 … 사냥할 때 links two uses of the same trick, one defensive and one offensive, so whatever fills the blank has to be the hunting counterpart of hiding from predators. An option that is not about being unseen cannot be the other half of that pair.

③ is the trap for people who know the animal. Fur does keep a fox warm and 체온을 유지하다 is a true sentence about arctic foxes — but the passage discusses 색깔, and a colour does not warm anything. True of the subject and absent from the text is the commonest wrong answer in this type.

① and ④ have no footing in the passage at all: nothing is said about company or about tracks. ① also runs against what little the paragraph implies, since an animal described as hiding itself is not being described as one that gathers into packs.
items.grammar:
N에 따라 is varying with N — 계절에 따라 색깔이 바뀐다. It attaches to a noun; for a whole clause you need -(으)ㅁ에 따라.

바꾸다 and 바뀌다 are the transitive and intransitive halves of one change, and this passage uses both a sentence apart: 여우가 색깔을 바꾸다 is the fox changing it, 색깔이 바뀌다 is the colour changing. The pair to learn alongside 늘리다/늘다 and 줄이다/줄다.

N(으)로부터 marks a source you move away from: 천적으로부터 보호하다, 부모로부터 독립하다. With a person in conversation Korean prefers 에게서.

숨길 곳이 없는 puts a modifier on 곳 and then denies the place exists — nowhere to hide. The same frame gives 할 말이 없다, 갈 데가 없다.

몰래 is without being noticed, and it stands directly in front of its verb: 몰래 다가가다, 몰래 보다. It is an adverb, so nothing attaches to it.

items.phraseKo: 요즘 연필을 잡고 글씨를 반듯하게 쓰는 것에 어려움을 느끼는 아이가 많다.

lines.ko: 요즘 연필을 잡고 글씨를 반듯하게 쓰는 것에 어려움을 느끼는 아이가 많다.
어린 나이부터 전자 기기를 장시간 사용한 탓이다.
전자 기기의 화면을 단순히 누르거나 미는 동작을 반복하다 보면 손에 있는 근육을 {} 못한다.
그래서 전문가들은 소근육이 발달하는 11세까지 손가락을 움직여서 하는 놀이를 많이 하도록 하는 것이 좋다고 말한다.

items.en: A lot of children now find it hard to hold a pencil and write neatly. It is because they have used electronic devices for long stretches from an early age. Keep repeating the simple press-or-swipe motion on a screen and the muscles in the hand do not get enough use. So specialists say it is good to have children do plenty of play that moves the fingers, up to the age of eleven while the fine muscles are developing.
items.why:
The blank sits in 근육을 ( ) 못한다, and 못한다 tells you before anything else that the sentence describes a failure. The paragraph's argument is already laid out: children cannot write neatly, because of long screen use, because pressing and swiping repeat one narrow motion. What that narrow motion fails to do is work the hand. ③.

The last sentence settles it from the other end. The recommendation is 손가락을 움직여서 하는 놀이를 많이 — plenty of play that moves the fingers — and a recommendation is only a remedy for the thing it supplies. More finger movement answers too little finger movement. On this type, reading the advice is often the fastest way to read the blank.

② uses the passage's own idea and points it the wrong way. Muscle being reduced is what the paragraph says is happening; 빠르게 줄이지 못한다 would mean the children are failing to reduce it, which is the opposite claim. Any option built from words already on the page is worth checking for direction before meaning.

④ assumes an injury the passage never gives — nothing has been damaged, so nothing is recovering. ① belongs to a different noun: 감싸다 is wrapping the hand around something, which is 연필을 잡고 from the first sentence, and it cannot take 근육을 as its object.

Worth noticing that all four options end in -지, because 못한다 follows the gap. The grammar is correct in every option, which is the usual state of affairs in this type and the reason it cannot be answered the way 문항 1-2 can.
items.grammar:
-(으)ㄴ 탓이다 gives a cause and blames it: 사용한 탓이다. Its neutral twin is 때문이다 and its grateful one 덕분이다, and choosing between the three is choosing an attitude rather than a meaning.

-다 보면 is keep doing it and eventually. 반복하다 보면 — the result comes from repetition rather than from one occasion. Keep it apart from -다 보니, which reports what was discovered after the fact rather than what will happen.

-거나 joins alternatives inside a clause: 누르거나 미는 동작, a pressing or swiping motion, with both verbs modifying 동작.

-지 못하다 is the long negative of inability, and it is not 안 하다. 사용하지 못한다 is cannot manage to use; 사용하지 않는다 would be chooses not to. The whole question turns on it being the first.

-도록 하다 is to see to it that someone does something, which is why the advice reads 놀이를 많이 하도록 하는 것이 좋다 rather than 놀이를 많이 하는 것이 좋다: the specialists are telling adults to arrange it for children.

items.phraseKo: 고인돌은 옛날 청동기 시대의 무덤이다.

lines.ko: 고인돌은 옛날 청동기 시대의 무덤이다.
고인돌은 받침돌 두 개를 세우고 그 위에 덮개돌을 얹은 형태인데 덮개돌 하나의 무게가 수십 톤에 달하는 것도 있다.
이와 같이 거대한 돌을 운반하고 세우려면 그만큼 많은 사람들의 힘이 필요했다.
그래서 고인돌은 사람들을 불러 모아 무덤 만드는 일을 시킬 수 있을 정도로 {} 사람의 무덤이었을 것으로 보인다.

items.en: A dolmen is a tomb from the Bronze Age. It is built by standing two support stones and laying a capstone across them, and a single capstone can weigh tens of tons. Carrying and raising a stone that size took the strength of a correspondingly large number of people. So a dolmen appears to have been the tomb of someone with power enough to call people together and set them to the work of building it.
items.why:
The blank takes the whole argument that came before it. Capstones run to tens of tons; moving and raising one needed many people; so the tomb belonged to someone who could 사람들을 불러 모아 … 일을 시킬 수 있을. Being able to summon people and set them to work is power, and ① says so.

정도로 is the hinge, and it is worth reading as an instruction. It measures the blank against the clause standing in front of it: to the degree that he could gather people and put them to work. So the blank must name something that would produce that ability, not something that merely sat alongside it.

③ is the outside-knowledge trap and the most tempting of the three, because 청동기 시대 brings bronze weapons to mind before the option is even read. But making weapons well is nowhere in the passage, and the passage argues from one thing only: the weight of the stone. Anything the paragraph has not measured cannot be what the paragraph concludes.

② and ④ both describe the buried person's body, which the passage never discusses, and neither would follow from a heavy tomb even if it did. ② additionally runs backwards: a paragraph about the labour a burial commanded is not building towards physical weakness.

The general rule this question teaches: when a blank follows 정도로, -(으)ㄹ 만큼 or -게, read the clause in front of it and ask what would cause it. What goes in the gap is a cause, not a description.
items.grammar:
N에 달하다 is to reach a figure, and the figure takes 에: 수십 톤에 달하다, 백만 명에 달하다. It belongs to writing and to news.

-(으)려면 is if you mean to. 운반하고 세우려면 … 힘이 필요했다 — the first clause is the intention and the second what it requires. It is the conditional that assumes someone wants the thing done.

-(으)ㄹ 정도로 is to the degree that. Whatever follows it is measured against the clause in front, which is exactly why it is where this question hides its work: 시킬 수 있을 정도로 대단한 권력.

-았을 것으로 보인다 is it appears to have been — a conclusion with a hedge on it, and the standard register for writing about the distant past. The paper uses it because the claim is inferred from stones rather than recorded.

시키다 is to make someone do a thing and takes 을/를 for the work itself: 일을 시키다, 숙제를 시키다. The general causative 하게 하다 puts the person in 에게 instead, and the two are not interchangeable here.

items.phraseKo: 오늘날의 연재 만화처럼 이야기가 회차별로 이어지는 작품의 형식은 이미 18세기에도 존재했다.

lines.ko: 오늘날의 연재 만화처럼 이야기가 회차별로 이어지는 작품의 형식은 이미 18세기에도 존재했다.
영국의 화가 윌리엄 호가스는 드라마 못지않게 흥미진진한 이야기를 여러 장의 그림으로 나누어 구성했다.
그리고 이를 판화에 새긴 후 {} 순서대로 인쇄해 판매했다.
독자들은 다음 회를 손꼽아 기다렸고 그의 그림을 보기 위해 기꺼이 돈을 지불했다.

items.en: The form we know from today's serialised comics — a story carried on instalment by instalment — already existed in the eighteenth century. The English painter William Hogarth composed stories as gripping as any drama, divided across several pictures. He then engraved them and printed and sold them in order, leaving a set interval between them. Readers counted the days until the next instalment and paid gladly to see his pictures.
items.why:
The passage is about serialisation and says so twice: 회차별로 이어지는 in the first sentence, 다음 회를 손꼽아 기다렸고 in the last. For readers to wait for a next instalment, the instalments have to appear apart in time, and ④ 일정한 기간을 두고 is what puts them apart.

The last sentence is the proof rather than a decoration. 손꼽아 기다리다 is counting the days on your fingers, and nobody counts days for something already in their hands. Had Hogarth printed and sold the whole set at once there would have been nothing to wait for and no reason for the sentence to exist.

③ contradicts that same sentence from the other side. 그의 그림을 보기 위해 — they paid to see his pictures, so they knew whose they were. 작가를 밝히지 않고 would make that impossible, and it uses a word the passage never raises.

① mistakes a comparison for an ambition. 오늘날의 연재 만화처럼 is the writer explaining an old form through a modern one; Hogarth was 영국의 화가 in the eighteenth century and was not trying to become a cartoonist, which did not yet exist as a job. ② is about orders, and nothing anywhere in the paragraph is.

Worth noticing where the deciding sentence is. The blank sits in the sentence about how he sold them, and what settles it is the sentence after, not the one before. On this type the evidence is very often downstream of the gap.
items.grammar:
N 못지않게 is no less than N: 드라마 못지않게 흥미진진한 이야기, a story as gripping as any drama. It attaches to a bare noun and modifies whatever follows.

N별로 is by each N — 회차별로 is instalment by instalment, and the same shape gives 나라별로, 학년별로. N대로 is as per N, so 순서대로 is in the order given, and 말대로, 계획대로 work the same way.

손꼽아 기다리다 is to count on the fingers while waiting, so to look forward to something keenly. It is fixed: 손꼽다 hardly appears without 기다리다 behind it.

-(으)ㄴ 후 is after, on a completed action: 새긴 후 인쇄했다. Its spoken twin is -고 나서, and -(으)ㄴ 뒤 is interchangeable with it.

기꺼이 is gladly, of something done without being pressed, and it collocates with paying, giving and helping: 기꺼이 돈을 지불하다, 기꺼이 돕다.

items.phraseKo: 사람들은 보통 식후에 바로 이를 닦는다.

lines.ko: 사람들은 보통 식후에 바로 이를 닦는다.
하지만 레몬 등 신맛이 강한 음식을 먹은 후에 바로 양치질을 하는 것은 좋지 않다.
신 음식에 있는 산성이 치아 보호막을 {} 때문에 바로 칫솔질로 자극하면 치아가 더 손상된다.
치아 보호막이 원래 강도로 돌아오려면 침으로 산성이 중화되어야 하는데 여기에 30분 정도가 소요된다.
그래서 신맛이 강한 음식을 섭취하면 최소 30분 이상 지나서 양치해야 한다.

items.en: People usually brush their teeth right after eating. But brushing straight after something sharply sour, lemon for instance, is not a good idea. The acid in sour food weakens the enamel for a while, so irritating it at once with a brush damages the teeth further. For the enamel to come back to its original hardness the acid has to be neutralised by saliva, and that takes about thirty minutes. So after eating something sharply sour you should wait at least thirty minutes before brushing.
items.why:
The sentence the blank sits in is a cause: 산성이 치아 보호막을 ( ) 때문에 … 치아가 더 손상된다. So the gap has to name what the acid does to the enamel that makes brushing harmful. ③ 일시적으로 약화시키기 — weakens it for a while.

The next sentence proves both halves of ③ separately, which is why it is there. 원래 강도로 돌아오려면 says the hardness has dropped and has to come back, and that is 약화. 30분 정도가 소요된다 says it does come back, and soon, and that is 일시적. The passage hands you the word and its qualifier one after the other.

④ describes what the 보호막 does rather than what the acid does to it, and it makes the sentence argue against itself: if the acid protected the enamel from food, brushing would not damage anything and there would be nothing to explain.

① and ② are inventions. Colour is never mentioned. And 여러 겹으로 만들기 would make the layer thicker — the opposite of a reason to leave the teeth alone for half an hour.

The paragraph is one piece of advice with its reason attached, and it closes on a number. When a passage ends in a figure, check whether the blank is the thing that figure measures: here the thirty minutes is exactly how long the weakening lasts.
items.grammar:
All four options end in -기 because the gap is followed by 때문에, which needs a noun in front of it. -기 때문에 is the nominalised cause; -아/어서 is the same idea on a clause and cannot take 때문에.

-시키다 makes a causative out of a 하다 noun: 약화하다 is to weaken, 약화시키다 is to make something weaken. 발전 and 안정 make the same pair, each with a 하다 form for the thing itself and a 시키다 form for causing it, and the 시키다 here is the same verb as question 18's 일을 시키다.

-(으)려면 is if it is to, and it sets up a requirement: 돌아오려면 … 중화되어야 하는데. Question 18 used it the same way with 운반하고 세우려면.

소요되다 is to be taken up, of time or money, and belongs to writing and to notices: 30분이 소요된다. In speech it is 30분이 걸린다.

최소 … 이상 stacks two words that each already mean at least, which reads as redundant and is perfectly normal in instructions. 섭취하다 is likewise the clinical word for eating, used wherever the writing is about nutrition rather than about meals.

items.phraseKo: 누군가에게 해를 입히고 미안한 척 거짓으로 흘리는 눈물을 '악어의 눈물'에 비유한다.

lines.ko: 누군가에게 해를 입히고 미안한 척 거짓으로 흘리는 눈물을 '악어의 눈물'에 비유한다.
실제로 악어는 먹잇감을 잡아먹으면서 눈물을 흘린다.
눈물샘을 담당하는 신경과 턱을 움직이는 신경이 연결되어 있기 때문에 음식을 씹을 때면 눈물이 나오는 것이다.
이 눈물 때문에 악어는 마치 다른 동물을 잡아먹으면서 {} 것처럼 보인다.
'악어의 눈물'이라는 표현은 인간의 가식적인 행위를 악어의 생리적 현상에 비유한 것이다.

items.en: Tears shed falsely, in feigned apology by someone who has done another harm, are likened to "crocodile tears". Crocodiles really do shed tears while eating their prey. The nerve that serves the tear gland and the nerve that moves the jaw are connected, so tears come when the animal chews. Because of those tears a crocodile looks as though it feels guilty while eating another creature. The phrase "crocodile tears" likens a piece of human pretence to a crocodile's physiology.
items.why:
The first sentence defines the idiom and the last one restates it, and the blank sits between them with both ends pinned. 미안한 척 거짓으로 흘리는 눈물 above it says the human version is feigned remorse; 인간의 가식적인 행위 below it says the same thing again. So what the crocodile appears to feel has to be the sincere version of that pretence — remorse. ② 죄책감을 느끼는.

④ is the interesting wrong answer, because it is the one that could actually be true. An animal finishing a meal may well be pleased about it. That is exactly what rules it out: the idiom exists to describe a feeling that is *not* real, and an option naming a genuine one cannot be what 가식적 is pointing at.

③ takes the tears literally in the other direction — tears are water, so perhaps it looks like drinking. But the paragraph has already given the physiology in full: the tear-gland nerve and the jaw nerve are wired together, and chewing sets them off. Thirst is not in it.

① has nobody frightened. The crocodile is the one doing the eating, and fear appears nowhere in these five sentences.

The shape to carry away: when a passage defines an expression at the top and explains the comparison at the bottom, a blank in the middle is almost always the definition said once more, in the terms of whatever the expression is compared to.
items.grammar:
-(으)ㄴ 척하다 is to pretend: 미안한 척하다, 모르는 척하다. The 척 can stand on its own in front of the next verb, which is what it does here — 미안한 척 거짓으로 흘리는.

마치 … -는 것처럼 is as if, and the two halves belong together: 마치 opens it and -는 것처럼 closes it. Neither is complete without the other in careful writing.

A를 B에 비유하다 is to liken A to B, with 에 on the thing being compared to. The passage uses it at both ends — 눈물을 악어의 눈물에 비유한다, then 행위를 현상에 비유한 것이다 — which is how the paragraph closes its own frame.

담당하다 takes 을/를: 눈물샘을 담당하는 신경, the nerve responsible for the tear gland. 연결되다 is the passive of 연결하다, so the nerves are wired together rather than wiring anything.

-적 turns a Sino-Korean root into a describing word — 가식적, 생리적 — and it needs -인 before a noun: 가식적인 행위. Without a noun after it, it stands bare: 생리적 현상 is the exception that proves how loose the rule is in practice.

items.phraseKo: 음료수 병과 같이 액체를 담는 용기들은 대부분 원기둥 모양이다.

lines.ko: 음료수 병과 같이 액체를 담는 용기들은 대부분 원기둥 모양이다.
원기둥을 선택하는 가장 큰 이유는 {} 위해서이다.
예를 들어 음료수 병의 밑면이 정사각형, 정삼각형, 원일 경우를 비교해 보자.
밑면의 넓이가 똑같이 100cm²일 때 둘레는 각각 40cm, 46cm, 35cm 정도로 원의 둘레가 가장 짧다.
따라서 같은 양의 액체를 담는 조건이라면 둘레를 감싸는 재료가 가장 적게 드는 원기둥으로 만들어 생산비를 낮추고자 하는 것이다.

items.en: Containers that hold liquid, drinks bottles among them, are mostly cylinders. The main reason for choosing a cylinder is to cut the cost of making the container. Compare a bottle whose base is a square, an equilateral triangle and a circle. With the base area the same 100cm² in each case, the perimeters come to about 40cm, 46cm and 35cm — the circle's is the shortest. So, holding the same volume of liquid, a cylinder needs the least material around its side, and making it that way brings the production cost down.
items.why:
위해서이다 follows the gap, so the blank is a purpose, and the last sentence states that purpose in as many words: 재료가 가장 적게 드는 원기둥으로 만들어 생산비를 낮추고자. Less material, lower production cost. ④.

The middle of the paragraph is the arithmetic that gets there, and it is worth reading as an argument rather than as numbers. Same base area, 100cm² in every case; perimeters of 40, 46 and 35; the circle is shortest. A shorter perimeter is less material wrapped round the side, and material is money.

①, ② and ③ are all perfectly true of a round bottle. It does look better, it does store more conveniently, and it is easier to hold. Not one of them is measured or argued for anywhere in the passage, which measures exactly one thing: perimeter. Only cost follows from perimeter.

That is the same trap question 16 set with 체온을 적절히 유지할 — an option true of the subject and absent from the reasoning. On this type the test is never whether a statement is true; it is whether this paragraph got there.

Read what comes after the gap before reading the options. 위해서이다 wants a purpose, 때문에 wants a cause, 것처럼 보인다 wants an appearance. The grammar behind the blank tells you what kind of thing you are looking for, and it is why all four options here end in -기.
items.grammar:
이유는 … -기 위해서이다 is a frame: the reason is in order to. It binds a reason to a purpose, and it is what forces the blank into a -기 form. Left as -기 위해서 alone the sentence would not close.

예를 들어 is for example, and the 들다 in it is the citing sense — 예를 들다, 손을 들다 — not the one three lines later.

들다 for cost takes the thing spent as its subject: 재료가 적게 들다, 돈이 많이 들다, 시간이 들다. The spender does not appear, which is why the sentence reads as a property of the shape rather than of the manufacturer.

N(이)라면 is if it is a case of N: 조건이라면, under that condition. It sets up the comparison the last sentence concludes from.

-고자 하다 is intends to, in writing, and it closes the paragraph the way 위해서이다 opened it. The 유사 표현 set already paired -고자 with -기 위해서; here both appear in one passage, four sentences apart.

exercises.instructionEn: Read the passage and answer both questions.
exercises.blurbEn: One passage answering two questions: something cut out of the text, and a second question about the passage as a whole.
exercises.noteEn:
From 문항 19 on, a passage carries two questions rather than one, and the two want opposite kinds of reading. The first is a gap in the text, decided by the sentences on either side of it and nothing else. The second is about the passage as a whole — its 주제, or which statement agrees with it — and is decided by everything except the sentence you are looking at.

Do the gap first, and do it locally.

Where the gap takes a connective, read the clause before it and the clause after it and name the relation. Two benefits in a row want 또한 or 게다가. A reversal wants 반면 or 그러나. 비록 is never alone — it needs -지만 or -더라도 later in its own sentence, so its absence rules 비록 out before you have weighed any meaning.

Where the gap takes an idiom, all four options will be body parts and only one of them will be about the right feeling. Sort them by whose feeling they describe: 눈살을 찌푸리다 is other people disapproving of what they see, 코가 납작해지다 is the subject being humbled, 한숨을 돌리다 is relief after strain, 목이 빠지다 is waiting. Then ask whose feeling the sentence needs. 행동이 … 한다 with a causative -게 하다 needs an effect on somebody else, which halves the list on grammar alone.

Then do the second question, and do it globally. Its wrong options fail in a small number of ways.

1. A true detail promoted to the theme, when the question asks for a 주제. 도로 침수 is in the passage, as one of the problems being solved rather than the point of it.

2. The direction reversed, when the question asks what agrees with the passage. Visitors increasing becomes visitors decreasing; the visitors blocking traffic becomes the city banning it. Both use the passage's own words, which is what makes them read well.

3. A word from the passage in a claim it never makes, or something plausible with no sentence behind it at all. 오염 beside groundwater, 식당이 없어 beside a street of restaurants.

For a 주제 question, the answer almost always names whatever the passage introduced with 그런데 or 최근. For an agreement question, take each option to the one sentence it is about and compare only those two.

items.en: City roads are mostly covered in asphalt, which water cannot soak through. So when it rains, the rainwater does not drain well into the ground: groundwater runs short, and roads flood often. Recently, though, a road surfacing material that water passes through easily has been developed. It is full of fine holes, so rainwater goes straight through and the groundwater supply is replenished. It also means less water rushing into the drains, so the risk of roads flooding falls as well.
items.why:
The gap takes 또한. The sentence before it says the new surface replenishes groundwater; the sentence after says less water floods the drains, so roads flood less. Both are benefits of the same material, so the relation is addition, and 또한 is the word for a second item of the same kind.

반면 is the trap, and the only one worth weighing. It marks a contrast, and there is a surface reason to expect one — the paragraph did open on a problem. But by this point the problem is two sentences behind and both clauses around the gap are advantages. What decides it is the pair either side of the gap, never the shape of the paragraph as a whole.

비록 can be ruled out without reading for meaning at all: it needs -지만 or -더라도 later in its own sentence, and there is none. 과연 is a speaker's reaction — sure enough, I wonder — and belongs to speech rather than to an explanatory paragraph.

The 주제 is ④. The passage is built as a problem and its answer: asphalt keeps water out, so groundwater runs short and roads flood; a new permeable material fixes both. ④ names the new material and both problems, which is the whole shape of the paragraph in one sentence.

③ is the detail promoted to a theme. 도로 침수 is genuinely in the passage, but as one of the two things being solved, and an option that restates a single sentence is a detail rather than a point. ① uses 오염, which is nowhere in the text — a word that sounds at home beside groundwater and rain, and is simply absent. ② says something reasonable about paving varying by city; no sentence here says it.

The quick route to a 주제: find what the passage introduced with 그런데 or 최근. Here it is 새 포장재, and the three sentences after it exist to explain what it does. That is the theme, and ④ is the only option built round it.
items.grammar:
또한 adds a second item of the same kind and belongs to writing; 게다가 is its spoken cousin and carries a hint of piling on. 반면 marks a contrast and usually takes -(으)ㄴ 반면 on a clause. 비록 must be answered later in the sentence by -지만 or -더라도, so a sentence without one cannot be taking 비록. 과연 is the speaker reacting — 과연 그렇구나 — and does not join two facts.

스며들다 is to soak through, and it takes the thing soaked in with 에: 물이 땅에 스며들다. 통과하다 is to pass through and takes 을/를. The passage uses both of the same water.

-아/어지다 turns an adjective into a change of state: 부족하다 is to be short, 부족해지다 is to become short. The same shape gives 많아지다, 좋아지다, and it is why the sentence reads 부족해지고 rather than 부족하고.

뒤덮여 있다 is -아/어 있다 on a passive: covered over, and still in that state. Keep it apart from 뒤덮고 있다, which would mean something is doing the covering right now.

줄다 and 줄어들다 are both to decrease, with 줄어들다 the more gradual of the two, and the passage uses one of each in the same sentence. -게 되다 on the end — 줄어들게 된다 — says the decrease comes about as a result rather than because anyone arranged it.

items.en: A street in Inju has become known as a food alley, packed with restaurants and cafés, and the number of people going there has risen lately. But some visitors behave in ways that make others frown: blocking traffic to take photographs in the middle of the road, setting up tripods on the pedestrian crossing to film. Near-accidents caused by filming without watching for cars have become common, and quarrels between drivers and visitors are growing more frequent too.
items.why:
The gap takes 눈살을 찌푸리게. The behaviour described just before it — blocking traffic, photographing in the middle of the road, tripods on the crossing — is behaviour other people disapprove of, and 눈살을 찌푸리다 is exactly that disapproval: the frown on the face of whoever is watching.

The grammar halves the list before any of the idioms are weighed. 행동이 ( ) 한다 is a causative: the behaviour makes somebody do something. So the idiom in the gap has to describe an effect on other people, and only 눈살을 찌푸리다 and 코가 납작해지다 can be caused in someone at all. 목이 빠지다 and 한숨을 돌리다 are states you fall into, not states an action puts other people in.

코가 납작해지다 is then wrong on meaning: it is being humbled, taken down a peg, and it happens to the person who was overconfident. Bad behaviour in a street does not humble the onlookers. 한숨을 돌리다 is relief after a strain and 목이 빠지다 is waiting a long time for something — neither has anything to do with what the paragraph describes.

The second question is ③. 운전자와 방문객 간에 다투는 일도 잦아지고 있다 is the last clause of the passage, and 갈등이 늘고 있다 is that same fact in plainer words: quarrels growing more frequent is conflict increasing.

① and ② are the passage's own words pointed the wrong way. Visitors are 늘고 있다, not 줄어들었다. And it is the visitors who 차량 통행을 막고 — the blocking is something they do, not something 인주시 decided; nothing in the passage says the city banned anything. An option built from words already on the page is always worth checking for direction and for who is doing what.

④ contradicts the first sentence outright: the street is a 먹거리 골목 where 식당과 카페가 모인, so 식당이 없어 is the opposite of what it says.
items.grammar:
Four body-part idioms, and they are worth learning as a set because this slot keeps asking for them. 눈살을 찌푸리다 is to frown in disapproval — the 눈살 is the skin between the brows. 코가 납작해지다 is to have your nose flattened, meaning to be humbled after boasting. 한숨을 돌리다 is to let a sigh out, so to get a breather once the worst has passed. 목이 빠지다 is to have your neck fall off from craning, so to wait and wait — 목이 빠지게 기다리다.

-게 하다 is the causative: 눈살을 찌푸리게 하다 is to make someone frown. It is what forces the gap to hold an idiom about other people, and it is the same -게 하다 the 빈칸 questions of 문항 1-2 set against -게 되다.

-(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 is came close to happening and did not. 사고가 날 뻔한 상황 is a situation where there nearly was an accident, and the -았/었 form 뻔했다 is how it is usually reported.

N 간에 is between N, and it belongs to writing where speech would say 사이에: 운전자와 방문객 간에. Both appear in this question, one in the passage and one in the options, which is how the paper checks you know they are the same thing.

-아/어지다 again, twice: 잦아지다 is 잦다 becoming, so growing more frequent, and 납작해지다 is 납작하다 becoming. The pattern turns a description into a change, which is why both belong to a paragraph about something getting worse.
